evidence.note: CLAIM: policy.window_start anchors the standing window on the latest standing-rule fire ONLY; so once standing_window_s passes with no new fire, window_start stays >0 forever and _window_open is permanently False -- no answer can fire again and no operator action (re-arming the window choice) reopens it. FALSIFIER (refutes the bug-claim): an ask.answered row answered with the standing-window choice (opened_window=True) re-anchors window_start, so the window reopens. CHEAP TEST ran (worktree .venv python): built a State with an opened_window=True ask row (answered_at 2026-01-01, verb complete.force, policy False) -> PO.window_start = 1767225600.0; the identical row with opened_window=False -> 0.0. CONFIRMED: opened_window re-anchors, a plain approve does not.

Implemented window reopen (B6e5e17ccda): ask.engine.answer() gained window:bool kwarg recording opened_window on ask.answered (commit 99701b49d, folded by core.handlers.asks h_requested default False + h_answered); policy.window_start anchors on max(in-scope policy fires UNION operator window-choice opens) via (r["policy"] or r["opened_window"]); harness.attest sets opened_window = hit.answer==window_label(ask_id) and repo is not None (commit 64e9f9570). Regression tests added in tests/test_approvals_policy.py.

data.probe: Committed code ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:168-171 reads `if r["answered_at"] and r["verb"] in cfg.approvals.standing_verbs and (r["policy"] or r["opened_window"]) and r["answered_by"] != "policy:auto-after-retries"`. There is NO redundant leading r["policy"] term: the fix REPLACED the original leading `if r["policy"]` with the (r["policy"] or r["opened_window"]) disjunction, so an operator re-open (policy False, opened_window True) IS included. Probed: worktree .venv window_start returns 1767225600.0 for an opened_window=True policy=False row, 0.0 for a plain approve; regression test test_the_window_choice_reopens_a_lapsed_window asserts the reopen fires again.

chunk_findings.detail: The condition `if r["policy"] and r["answered_at"] and r["verb"] in cfg.approvals.standing_verbs and (r["policy"] or r["opened_window"])` uses `r["policy"]` redundantly on both sides of the `and`, rendering `r["opened_window"]` completely unreachable because `r["policy"]` evaluates to `True` for policy fires and `False` for operator answers that set `opened_window=True`. Given a logged answer where `r["policy"]` is `False` and `r["opened_window"]` is `True`, the expression `r["policy"] and ...` evaluates to `False`, so operator re-opens are never included in `starts` and lapsed windows are never re-opened.
